seoTitle: Free Random JSON Generator - Nested, Seeded
metaDescription: Generate random nested JSON with a chosen depth, width and seed. Useful for testing parsers, formatters and UIs. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Create random but repeatable JSON documents. Set how deep it nests, how many keys or items each level has, and the seed.
why:
Testing a JSON viewer, a diff tool, a parser or a table component needs input with real variety: nested objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and nulls. Hand-writing that structure takes time, and copying a real payload may expose private data.

This generator builds a document from scratch each time. Depth controls how far it nests, width caps the number of keys or items per level, and the seed makes the result repeatable, so a bug report can say which seed triggered it. You can pick the indentation, including none for a compact payload. Values include integers, decimals, short phrases, UUID-style strings and null. Use it for fuzzing, benchmarking formatters or filling a demo screen quickly.
howTo: Set the maximum number of keys or items per level, from 1 to 8.
Enter a seed to repeat a result, and choose the indent.

faq.q: Is the output always the same for the same seed?
faq.a: Yes. The same seed, depth and width return the same document every time. Change the seed to get a different structure. Numeric seeds are used directly and text seeds are hashed into a number.

faq.q: How big can the output get?
faq.a: Depth 6 with width 8 can grow into thousands of values, because each level may branch. For small samples keep depth at 3 or 4. The limits are capped at 6 and 8 to protect your browser.
Yes, the output is produced by JSON.stringify, so it parses anywhere. Setting indent to 0 gives a single compact line, useful for size tests.

faq.q: Can I define my own fields?
faq.a: Not here. This tool makes arbitrary structures. If you need specific field names and types such as email or date, use the mock data generator, which takes a schema.
